benchmark: agent hook wall-clock latency, one-shot (every lookup is a fresh axil process)
label: one-shot baseline (no daemon)

uncommitted_changes.note: not recorded: this run predates the field. axil_version ends in -dirty, so the binary was built from a checkout with uncommitted changes to tracked files and is not exactly git_commit

machine: Apple M1 Pro, 10 cores, 16 GiB, macOS 26.6

corpus.database: copy of benchmarks/dogfood-recall/data/snap-prefix (frozen copy of this repo's .axil)

method.command: axil hook run --dialect claude, payload on stdin
method.timing: whole hook process wall clock, python perf_counter around subprocess.run
method.session_ids: fresh per sample, so no per-session sentinel skips a lookup
method.validation: a sample counts only if its lookup ran (output or sentinel checked); a prompt recall that returns nothing after its 1800 ms --timeout-ms counts, as a deadline_hit

freshness_scan.method: crates/extensions/axil-indexer/examples/freshness_timing.rs on the same copy and tree: the calls recall (stale_file_paths) and boot (check_freshness) make

budget_share.derived_from: stale_file_paths_ms above and cases.user_prompt_recall.p50_ms of this run (2026-09-29T03:02:14Z, 65d45ff), by the formula in scripts/daemon-latency.sh; computed after the run, not re-measured
budget_share.note: share_of_warm_gate_budget is the scan's warm p50 and p95 over the 50 ms p50 gate (the gate has no p95 bound); the scan grows with the tree (it scans 433 of the tree's 617 files here). Whether a warm process needs a freshness cache is decided on its own warm numbers, not on this one-shot run. one_shot_scan_ms is the first call in a process (one sample), about what each one-shot hook pays.
